# Parameterised reports {#sec-m5-parametrizados}

A parameterised report is a template with "holes": the municipality, the segment, the year, the scenario.
You render the same file several times, changing the parameter, and get one report per
case, all with the same structure and the same methodology.

It is the answer to the recurring request: *"do this same study for the other 27 corridors"*.

This chapter turns the Paranaguá report from the previous chapter
(@sec-relatorio-paranagua) into a template, and renders it for the five municipalities with the most
coastal shipping in the country.

## From report to template

The Paranaguá report was written with this in mind: the municipality appears in a single block, at the
start, and everything else uses the variables `municipio`, `uf` and `codigo`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
municipio <- "Paranaguá"
uf        <- "PR"
```

Parameterising is replacing these fixed values with **parameters**, declared in the document's
header. The rest of the report does not change a single line.

## Declaring the parameters

In the template document's YAML:

```yaml
---
title: "Municipal profile: `r knitr::inline_expr("params$municipio")` (`r knitr::inline_expr("params$uf")`)"
params:
  municipio: "Paranaguá"
  uf: "PR"
---
```

The YAML values are the defaults, used when nobody provides others. Inside the document,
they are in the `params` list, and the report's first block becomes:

```{r}
#| eval: false
municipio <- params$municipio
uf        <- params$uf
```

During development, it is handy to simulate the parameters so that you can run the code line by
line in the console, where `params` does not exist:

```{r}
# during development; when rendered, `params` comes from the YAML
if (!exists("params")) params <- list(municipio = "Paranaguá", uf = "PR")

params$municipio
```

## The complete template

The finished template, which is the Paranaguá chapter with the first block replaced by the parameters,
is in [`modelo_perfil.qmd`](../modelos/modelo_perfil.qmd) (in Portuguese). Save it in the **root of the course project**
(the folder that contains `dados/`), because it reads `dados/cabotagem_tku_2025.xlsx` through a relative
path.

For one municipality, render it passing the parameters in `execute_params`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
quarto::quarto_render(
  input          = "modelo_perfil.qmd",
  output_file    = "perfil_manaus_AM.html",
  execute_params = list(municipio = "Manaus", uf = "AM")
)
```

Without `execute_params`, the YAML defaults apply, and you get the Paranaguá report.

## Rendering for five municipalities

The cases come from the data themselves: the five municipalities with the most coastal shipping TKU, adding up
outbound and inbound.

```{r}
library(dplyr)

colunas <- c("ano", "perfil", "sh2",
             "pais_origem", "uf_origem", "cidade_origem", "instalacao_origem",
             "pais_destino", "uf_destino", "cidade_destino", "instalacao_destino",
             "tku")

cabotagem <- readxl::read_excel("dados/cabotagem_tku_2025.xlsx", na = c("", "-"))
names(cabotagem) <- colunas

cabotagem <- cabotagem |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.character), stringr::str_squish)) |>
  dplyr::filter(tku > 0)

casos <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cabotagem |> dplyr::select(cidade = cidade_origem,  uf = uf_origem,  tku),
  cabotagem |> dplyr::select(cidade = cidade_destino, uf = uf_destino, tku)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(cidade)) |>                    # EEZ/platforms are not municipalities
  dplyr::summarise(tku_bi = sum(tku) / 1e9, .by = c(cidade, uf)) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(tku_bi, n = 5)

casos |> knitr::kable(digits = 1,
                      col.names = c("Municipality", "State", "TKU (billion t·km)"))
```

And the loop that produces one report per row of `casos`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
dir.create("resultados/relatorios", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(casos))) {
  municipio <- casos$cidade[i]
  uf        <- casos$uf[i]

  # perfil_sao_luis_MA.html: no accents or spaces in the file name
  arquivo_saida <- paste0(
    "perfil_",
    municipio |> stringr::str_to_lower() |> stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") |>
      stringr::str_replace_all("[^a-z]+", "_"),
    "_", uf, ".html"
  )

  message("Rendering ", municipio, " (", i, "/", nrow(casos), ")")

  quarto::quarto_render(
    input          = "modelo_perfil.qmd",
    output_file    = arquivo_saida,
    execute_params = list(municipio = municipio, uf = uf)
  )

  file.rename(arquivo_saida, file.path("resultados/relatorios", arquivo_saida))
}
```

Each report takes about two minutes, most of it filtering the Census tables for the whole
country. The Census files and the boundaries are downloaded only on the first render; on the
following ones, they come from the computer.

Some details that avoid frustration:

- `output_file` must be just the file **name**, not a path. Hence the `file.rename()`
  afterwards.
- The municipality name must be written as in IBGE, with accents: it is how the template
  finds the IBGE code. In the coastal shipping dataset, the names already follow that spelling.
- Renders in a series reuse little; if the data preparation is heavy, do it **before**
  the loop and save an `.rds` that the template only reads.
- Wrap the call in `tryCatch()` when the cases come from a long list: one municipality
  without data should not stop the other 27.

```{r}
#| eval: false
resultados <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(casos)), function(i) {
  tryCatch({
    quarto::quarto_render("modelo_perfil.qmd",
                          execute_params = list(municipio = casos$cidade[i], uf = casos$uf[i]))
    data.frame(caso = casos$cidade[i], status = "ok")
  }, error = function(e) {
    data.frame(caso = casos$cidade[i], status = paste("error:", e$message))
  })
})

dplyr::bind_rows(resultados)
```

This status table is the "report of the report": in a run of 27 documents, it tells you
which came out and which failed, without you having to check the folder file by file.

## An index of the reports produced

```{r}
#| eval: false
arquivos <- list.files("resultados/relatorios", pattern = "\\.html$")

indice <- data.frame(
  arquivo = arquivos,
  link = paste0("[", stringr::str_remove(arquivos, "\\.html$"), "](", arquivos, ")")
)

writeLines(c("# Reports by municipality", "", indice$link),
           "resultados/relatorios/index.md")
```

With this, the delivery stops being a folder with 27 loose files and becomes a browsable
set that, published on GitHub Pages, becomes a permanent reference portal.

## When to parameterise

| Situation | Worth it? |
|:--|:--|
| Same study for many units (municipalities, segments, corridors) | yes, clearly |
| Recurring report (monthly, quarterly) with a fixed structure | yes, the parameter is the period |
| Scenarios of the same analysis | yes, the parameter is the scenario |
| A one-off document, made once | no; parameterising costs more than it pays |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Automating the recurrence

A monthly report can be scheduled: on Windows, with Task Scheduler, calling
`Rscript -e 'quarto::quarto_render("relatorio.qmd")'`; on a Linux server, with `cron`; or on
GitHub itself, with a scheduled *workflow*, the same mechanism that publishes this site. The data
are updated at the source, and the report arrives ready.
:::
